title: FP8 profile activation checklist and fallback procedures for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We have validated FP8 kernels for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2) across a set of offline workloads but still need a hardened activation plan for production. This ticket captures an activation checklist, canary gating metrics, calibration dataset and validation steps, plus deterministic fallback procedures to INT8 or previous FP16/FP32 profiles.

Goal: Safely enable the FP8 profile for selected models on Hopper nodes with minimal customer impact and clear rollback criteria. Provide a repeatable checklist for SRE/ML infra to run canaries and for Eng to triage stability issues.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary activation automation that ramps traffic and evaluates the quality and reliability metrics described below.
- Calibration job that produces stable E4M3/E5M2 scale/clipping parameters (seeded, version-controlled) and a signed artifact in storage.
- Telemetry and dashboards to show P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, token rejection rate, per-route quality deltas, and kernel-level OOM/fatal counts.
- Defined rollback triggers and automatic fallback path to INT8/FP16 with zero downtime.
- Playbook steps documented in Confluence and linked from the Canary UI.

Calibration dataset and validation:
- Use the calibration corpus (10k prompts) covering short/medium/long sequences, multiple token distributions, and edge cases (long context, heavy numeric content, code). Dataset: s3://redwood-calibration/fp8/hopper/corpus-v2025-02 (MD5 and SHA256 pinned).
- Calibration runs must be reproducible: docker image runtime:gpu:2025.02-calib, seed=42, max-seqs-per-batch=32, kv-cache warming enabled.
- Validate calibration by running the holdout set (2k prompts) and computing: token-level log-prob delta, output token edit distance, and human-eval pass-rate proxy (automated reference checks). Thresholds: relative logprob delta <= 0.5%, automated pass-rate degradation <= 0.8% absolute.

Canary ramp and gating thresholds:
- Ramp schedule: 0.1% traffic (6 hours) -> 1% (12 hours) -> 5% (24 hours) -> 25% (48 hours) -> 100% (after approval).
- Acceptance window: use rolling 3-hour windows for quality; use 1h windows for reliability/latency.
- Gating thresholds (fail open if exceeded -> automatic rollback):
  - Latency P99 > baseline + 30ms for two consecutive windows.
  - Error rate (5xx / request) > 0.5% absolute increase.
  - Kernel OOMs or fatal GPU resets > 1 per 10k tokens.
  - Quality regression: automated metric shows > 1.0% absolute degradation or logprob delta > 1.0%.

Fallback procedures:
- Immediate soft-fallback: route affected sessions to INT8 profile of same model (if exists) while preserving routing headers. Route shift should be gradual (roll-back ramp: 100% of canary segment over 5 minutes) to avoid spikes.
- Hard rollback: remove FP8 profile from serving config and re-deploy traffic policy. Post-mortem required within 48 hours.
- Maintain artifact versions for both FP8 and INT8 profiles. The serving runtime must accept model_profile_version headers to pin to working artifact.

Telemetry and tracing:
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/qa/fp8-canary
- Traces: configure per-request trace id propagation and include model_profile, kernel_variant, gpu_uuid in spans.
- Alerts: create PagerDuty policy for noise-filtered criticals (latency regressions, kernel resets).

Operational runbook snippets:
- Pre-canary checklist: ensure calibration artifacts exist, GPU firmware up-to-date (driver >= 510.xx), scheduler config pinned, and autoscaler policies warmed.
- During canary: monitor the 5 gating metrics and manually inspect 50 failed generations with high edit-distance.
- Post-canary: run full-house regression (overnight) against the validation harness and black-box human eval slices for high-risk customers.

Engineering notes and trade-offs:
- Trade-off between aggressiveness of E4M3 vs E5M2: E4M3 favored for throughput; E5M2 favored when corner-case numeric stability observed. We will prefer E5M2 for models with high numeric sensitivity (LLM-finance, LLM-code) and E4M3 for chat/QA where throughput is prioritized.
- Batching interactions: large continuous batching can amplify quantization drift. Canary nodes will run a bounded-batching policy (max_batch_ms=12ms) to reduce tail effects.
- KV cache warming: pre-warm cache for long-context tests to catch scale/overflow patterns early.

Links and artifacts:
- Calibration artifacts: s3://redwood-calibration/fp8/hopper/artifacts/ENG-75420/
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/FP8+Hopper+Calibration
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824 (canary automation), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1849 (profile selector), https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/557 (canary dashboard panels)

Next steps:
1) Complete automation PR and get eng review (owner: @jonahk).
2) Run two calibration runs using corpus-v2025-02 and publish artifacts.
3) Kick off first canary for model-family A (low-risk) and monitor for 72 hours.
4) If stable, expand to model-family B and run human-eval slice.

Note: If any quality gating is hit, capture the full request payloads (PII redaction) and open ENG-XXXX for a focused investigation.
